$comment: Allow-list record for the repo ROOT and docs/. scripts/check-manifest.mjs can validate it explicitly, but it is not a `pnpm gate` or CI rung. Adding a NEW top-level root entry, or a NEW standalone doc under docs/, REQUIRES adding it here with a justification first — that friction is the point: it blocks temp/ad-hoc junk at root and keeps durable project knowledge in the Library (definition/principle/pattern/guardrail/techstack/adr/open-question), not loose prose docs. A new doc's justification must say why it does NOT belong in the Library. See the `repo-surface-allowlist` Library guardrail.

packageOwnership.$comment: The organism-boundary ownership map (ADR-0074, amended by ADR-0075), read by packages/cli/src/check-boundaries.ts (`pnpm check:boundaries`, wired into `pnpm gate` + the CI verify job). Every @storytree/* package under packages/* is classified EXACTLY once as an `organism` (owned by one story). The gate asserts every real runtime cross-organism dependency edge (each package.json `dependencies`; devDeps are test scaffolding and excluded, ADR-0010 §5) is COVERED by a declared cross-story edge — consumer-side in the consumer story's `depends_on`, OR provider-side in the provider story's `consumed_by` (stories/*/story.md, ADR-0074 §4) — so cross-organism coupling can't be added without a declared edge, and because the studio forest renders `depends_on`, every coupling is therefore UI-visible. NOTE (ADR-0075, 2026-06-19; the ports renamed for role-not-position per ADR-0078, 2026-06-20): the shared ports storage-protocol/proof-protocol are NO LONGER an exempt `substrate` class — they are ordinary ROOT organisms (stories/storage-protocol + stories/proof-protocol, depends_on [] / [proof-protocol]) that every consumer DECLARES depends_on, exactly like cli/store stopped being exempt 'composition roots' in ADR-0074 §2. They stay listed in `foundational` (a SUBSET of organisms, not a class) to carry ONE minimality rule the gate enforces — a foundational port may only depend on another foundational port — which keeps them zod-only / node+pg-free so the studio's browser bundle works. So a port dependency is a visible declared+rendered edge, not an invisible exemption.
packageOwnership.$comment_surfaces: Consuming SURFACES (ADR-0100): a surface name → the story that owns it. A surface is an apps/* app (the studio) — a sink that wires organisms together and is consumed by nothing. ADR-0100 brought apps/* into the same boundary scan as packages/*: a surface's package.json @storytree/* deps are COVERED by the same rule as an organism's (declared in the surface's own story depends_on), so the studio's real wiring is enforced + rendered, exactly the visibility-over-exemption call ADR-0074 §2 made for the cli/store hubs. A surface is never `foundational` and draws no inbound edge. (The public-website subrepo is also a consuming surface but ships no workspace package — its forest-world edge is a declared story node backed by the check:web-engine drift gate, ADR-0093, not a package scanned here.)

sourceOwnership.$comment: The SECOND declared ownership map (ADR-0317 D2), at SUBTREE grain — the `packageOwnership` pattern one level down, read by packages/cli/src/ownership.ts (`storytree ownership`). `packageOwnership` above answers 'which story owns this PACKAGE' and check:boundaries holds it to the disk at 24/24. Nothing answered 'which addressable unit is responsible for this FILE', and the natural candidate cannot: `proof.real.sourceFile` is typed `sourceFile: string`, a total function unit→the one file that unit AUTHORS, so it inverts into ownership neither surjectively (its image is bounded by the 296-node count, not the 519 files) nor injectively (apps/studio/src/components/TreeView.tsx is named by SEVEN units). That field is NOT decayed — 111 owned against 117 declared-and-existing targets, ~95% full — it simply was never an ownership map, and `scope.sourceGlobs` is a per-phase WRITE FENCE deliberately broader than what a unit owns (which is why check-boundaries.ts:227 filters globs out of the proof-bound set). NEITHER field is read here and neither changes: the prove-it-gate, the phase machine, the write scopes and every signed verdict carry ZERO risk from this map. GLOBS ARE PERMITTED HERE and refused there, because this map binds no verdict. VALUE = an addressable object in the work graph: a CAPABILITY id by preference (the grain claims are taken at, ADR-0270 D1), or a story id where no capability is the honest answer; ADR-0317 D3 makes a declared subtree itself claimable. REPORT-ONLY: `storytree ownership` renders this and fails nothing, and a BLOCKING rung must earn its place on this report's own numbers first (ADR-0311 retired sixteen rungs for want of evidence). ### AUTHORED IN FULL 2026-08-06 (first-class-edges-arc), 527 of 527 files owned, and three authoring rules the next editor must keep. (1) MIXED GRAIN, WITH THE SPLIT REPORTED. Capability grain wherever a capability's stated outcome names or plainly covers the subtree's job; story grain only where the tree HAS no such capability. Measured on landing: 363 files (68.9%) capability-grain, 164 (31.1%) story-grain. Story grain is legal (ADR-0317 D3) but it satisfies totality while leaving 'claim the capability you are writing' nothing finer to bind to — which is the arc's founding measurement, now COUNTED instead of assumed. The residual IS the story-author worklist, it is OWNED, and it MOVES BOTH WAYS — ask `storytree ownership` for the live grain line rather than quoting a figure from here, because it drains as capabilities are authored and ACCRUES as new code lands story-grain. Re-measured 2026-08-07 BEFORE increment 2 landed against it: 372 of 537 files (69.3%) capability-grain, 165 (30.7%) story-grain, concentrated in `cli` 51 (gate rungs, drains, generated-view builders, doctors), `studio` 39, `desktop` 12 (increment 2 took that owner to 5 — see rule (5)), `app-surface` 8, `drive-machinery` 8. The owner is `capability-layer-coverage-arc` (chartered 2026-08-07): every story-grain declaration is resolved either into a capability that STATES ITS PROOF or into a recorded one-competence decision — and a count driven to zero by authoring unprovable capabilities is that arc's stated FAILURE mode, not its goal, so do NOT read a falling number here as progress on its own. Two of the story-grain owners are NOT gaps — `proof-protocol` (8) and `storage-protocol` (6) are root-port stories that carry no capabilities because the story IS the one competence. NO BLANKET BUCKET: every owner here names a real object in the work graph (`storytree ownership` resolves all 372 and reports 0 unresolved); an invented 'substrate' owner would drive the number down while changing nothing. (2) DECLARATIONS ARE DISJOINT — never a specific entry plus a broader one covering it. The judge collects EVERY match and reports a second one as CONTESTED regardless of key order, so the ordering-based 'specific before broad' pattern would light that warning permanently over 350+ files — every file sitting under a specific entry — and destroy the signal. Order is therefore free here and contested==0 means what it says. Use `<dir>/*.ts` for a non-recursive directory (`*` never crosses `/`) when a subdirectory needs a different owner; a bare `<dir>` claims everything beneath it and is right only where the whole tree is one competence (packages/forest-world/src, packages/procedural-architecture/src/buildings). (3) THE ENTRY COUNT IS 372, NOT 'tens'. ADR-0317 expected subtree grain to keep entries in the tens; measured, the economy holds where directories are homogeneous (24 packageOwnership entries; forest-world in one line) and breaks in FLAT, HETEROGENEOUS src/ directories where ownership genuinely varies file by file — packages/cli/src is 100 files fronting ~20 different organisms. 372:527 is what totality actually costs here. A new file lands UNOWNED and must be declared; that is the totality check working, and it is why no catch-all is left to swallow it silently. ### (4) A PACKAGE BARREL IS STORY GRAIN BY NATURE, NOT A GAP — added 2026-08-07 by capability-layer-coverage-arc increment 1, generalising rule (1)'s `proof-protocol`/`storage-protocol` note from whole stories down to individual subtrees. A `src/index.ts` that only re-exports its package's public surface is the STORY's front door: it is the union of every organ the package fronts, so no single capability is responsible for it and a capability that claimed it would be claiming its siblings' code. Declaring it at story grain is therefore the DECIDED answer, not a residue awaiting a capability — the same reasoning that makes a root-port story one competence, applied one level down. Recorded here rather than per-entry because the map is key→owner with no room for a note. Settled this way in increment 1: `packages/drive/src/index.ts`, `packages/orchestrator/src/index.ts`, `packages/orchestrator/src/store/index.ts`. The rule generalises — counted 2026-08-07, SIXTEEN story-grain declarations are bare `src/index.ts` barrels; the three named above are settled here and the remaining THIRTEEN sit across the long tail (`agent`, `library`, `app-surface`, `notice-board`, `model-uat*`, `uat-criterion`, `context-traversal-*`, `website-experience`), so that tail is decidable BY THIS RULE and does not need per-file judgment. THE RULE IS ABOUT RE-EXPORT BARRELS ONLY: an `index.ts` carrying real logic is ordinary code and gets the rule (1) treatment. READ IT AS THE DEFAULT ANSWER FOR A BARREL, NOT AS A CLAIM ABOUT WHAT THIS MAP ALREADY SAYS — one live declaration does not match it and is deliberately left alone: `packages/cli/src/index.ts` is a pure re-export barrel (26 lines, every line a re-export) yet is declared to the CAPABILITY `unified-command-dispatch`, alongside `main.ts`/`commands.ts`/`envelope.ts`. Whether to re-point it belongs to `capability-layer-coverage-arc`, not to this rule: re-pointing a declaration ahead of authoring the organ is the opening move that arc explicitly forbids. One more subtree was settled at story grain in increment 1 on the separate ground that it is not an ORGAN: `packages/drive/src/doctrine.ts`, 39 lines rendering one fail-soft CLI doctrine-pointer line, with no colocated test (it is exercised through the `packages/cli` shim). Authoring a capability over it would have breached the arc's hard constraint that a capability must state its own proof. ### (5) FOR A LODGER, COUNT THE CALL SITES BEFORE RE-HOMING IT — added 2026-08-07 by capability-layer-coverage-arc increment 2. A LODGER is code sitting in a package it reaches many consumers from rather than one the owning story is responsible for (increment 1 named the pattern in `packages/drive`; it is the dominant difficulty in the residue, and in `cli` and `studio` the question is usually 'WHICH STORY owns this?' rather than 'which capability?'). The tempting move is to re-home it to whichever story its file header or its originating survey names. That move is wrong often enough to need a check, and the check OPENS mechanically: ENUMERATE THE CALL SITES AND SEE WHAT FRACTION BELONG TO THE CANDIDATE STORY. Demonstrated on `apps/desktop/src/backend/open-link-policy.ts`, which this arc proposed re-homing to `embedded-terminal` on the strength of its header (it came from the embedded-terminal patterns survey) and a live precedent (`pty-session-manager` already owns a sibling file in that same directory). `story-author` refused: only ONE of its three call sites is terminal-scoped (`terminal:open-link`), while the other two — `will-navigate` and `setWindowOpenHandler` — are the whole-window navigation lockdown protecting every preload bridge (ADR-0109 §Decision 4). Re-homing would have filed the desktop shell's navigation lockdown under a story that draws no edge to the shell. A header names a module's ORIGIN; the call sites name its JOB, and ownership follows the job. Note the two findings are independent: the call-site count decides WHICH STORY, and the organ test then decides whether a capability exists there at all — this file failed the second too (37 lines, one pure predicate, three isolated unit tests, no integration proof available) and stayed at story grain under rule (1). TWO FENCES ON THIS RULE, both supplied by its own demonstration. THE FRACTION POINTS; THE READING DECIDES. 1-of-3 did not settle `open-link-policy.ts` by arithmetic — it settled it because the two non-terminal sites are a qualitatively DIFFERENT JOB, and their own comments say so: `main.ts:502` (`will-navigate`) and `:508` (`setWindowOpenHandler`) exist because the top frame 'must never be steered off the app's own origin' or an attacker link 'would otherwise inherit the shell-spawn bridge'. Re-verified on the bytes at HEAD 2026-08-07 by the pre-merge librarian pass rather than taken from this note: the enumeration is exactly three call sites and the split is exactly 1/2. A 2-of-3 split across call sites doing the SAME job would decide nothing, so never report the ratio without the reading that goes with it. AND THIS IS A JUDGMENT AID FOR WHAT TO DECLARE, NEVER A DERIVATION OF THE MAP. ADR-0317 D2 REJECTS deriving ownership from the import graph — it would encode who DEPENDS ON a file rather than who is RESPONSIBLE for it, would attribute shared substrate to all 45 stories, and its errors would be silent and indistinguishable from its correct answers — and that rejection stands here unweakened. What this rule licenses is reading the call sites of ONE lodger already under question, to inform a DECLARED answer; nothing is computed over the repo, and a session that reads it as 'derive the map from imports' has inverted the decision this map sits under. ### (6) A GATE INSTRUMENT HOMES TO THE STORY WHOSE TEST SURFACE GOES RED WHEN THE THING DRIFTS — added 2026-08-07 by capability-layer-coverage-arc increment 3, and recorded because it CORRECTS a plausible generalisation that increment itself proposed and `story-author` refuted. `packages/cli/src` hosts many check-gate instruments, and increment 3 opened by arguing from an apparent pattern: a gate instrument is homed to the story that owns the CHECKED THING rather than to `cli` — citing `check-process-graph.ts` -> `library-health-gate` (story `library`), `check-web-grounding.ts` -> `website`, `check-declared.ts` -> `claim-at-declare`, and `*boundaries*.ts` -> `organism-boundary-tooling`. THE PATTERN IS NOT UNIFORM, AND THE LAST CITATION BREAKS IT: `organism-boundary-tooling` is a capability of story `cli`, and it is the closest structural twin in the corpus to the case under question — a pure judge plus a check gatherer in `packages/cli/src`, sitting at the immediately adjacent step in `gate-order.ts`. Read as a rule about WHOSE SUBJECT MATTER the gate inspects, the precedent set is mixed and decides nothing. What actually carries is that precedent's OWN stated criterion: `organism-boundary-tooling` is homed to `cli` because it rides the CLI's test surface — `boundaries.test.ts` goes red when it breaks. So the operative question is not whose subject matter is inspected but WHOSE SUITE OBSERVES THE DRIFT: home the instrument where a drift makes a test go red, because binding an outcome to a suite that cannot fail on it is the rubber stamp ADR-0097 §2 forbids (§2 is captioned as RE-AFFIRMING ADR-0085, which is where the ban originates — cite the pair, not §2 alone; the same objection `stories/cli/story.md` raises when refusing to bind its own UAT leg 4 to `cli#gate-1`). Demonstrated on the cross-surface conformance harness — nine files, three story-grain declarations across `cli` / `studio` / `desktop`, one organ: `pnpm --filter @storytree/cli test` runs the judge's rules but NEVER SPAWNS A PROBE, so it cannot go red when the desktop's re-composed route table drifts from the studio's, which is the entire outcome. The only command that can is `pnpm check:mirror-conformance`, and the surface under obligation is the desktop's hand-written copy (all three MIRRORS rows are reference studio, mirror desktop), so the organ was authored as `mirrored-route-conformance` in story `desktop` and all three declarations re-pointed at it. FOUR FENCES. THIS RULE DECIDES WHERE AN INSTRUMENT LIVES AND IS DOWNSTREAM OF RULE (1), NEVER A SUBSTITUTE FOR IT — an instrument whose drift NO suite observes is not thereby homeless; it is a capability that CANNOT STATE ITS PROOF and must not be authored at all. AND A GATE'S GATHERER IS PART OF THE ORGAN ONLY WHEN IT MANUFACTURES OBSERVABILITY THAT DOES NOT OTHERWISE EXIST: the six probes here exist solely because ADR-0176 forbids importing across the wall, so nothing else can see the desktop's payload, and a per-surface split would have produced two units that print JSON and exit with no test file, no assertion and no observable — illegal under the same must-state-its-proof constraint. Contrast `check-boundaries.ts`, which only collects package.json facts anyone can read and is deliberately EXCLUDED from `organism-boundary-tooling` as glue. THIRD, AND ITS OWN DEMONSTRATION FORCES THIS ONE: THE SUITE CRITERION ELIMINATES, IT DOES NOT SELECT — read ‘test surface’ as ANY command that reds on the drift, NEVER as ‘a package suite’. Added 2026-08-07 by the pre-merge librarian pass that reviewed this rule. Applied literally as a SELECTOR the headline does not settle its own case: nothing that reds on a mirrored-payload drift is a story’s suite at all. `pnpm check:mirror-conformance` is a ROOT gate step, deliberately outside the ADR-0195 affected-only narrowing, and belongs to no story’s `--filter … test`. What the criterion actually did here was REFUTE `cli`; what SELECTED `desktop` was the OBLIGATION — all three registry rows are `reference: studio, mirror: desktop`, so the surface under obligation is the desktop’s hand-written copy. The observing command POINTS AWAY from a wrong home; the obligation decides the right one — the same shape as rule (5)’s THE FRACTION POINTS; THE READING DECIDES. This is not a nicety: read ‘suite’ as ‘package suite’ and fence 1 above turns on this rule, because a session would find that NO suite observes this drift and conclude the capability must not have been authored at all — refuting the very unit the rule was written to justify. FOURTH, THIS RULE GOVERNS OVER RULE (5) FOR AN INSTRUMENT, AND THE TWO GENUINELY CONFLICT ON THIS VERY CASE — recorded so the conflict is not rediscovered later as a contradiction. Rule (5) says the CALL SITES decide which story. Enumerated on the bytes 2026-08-07: `mirror-conformance.ts` has exactly THREE call sites and ALL THREE are in `packages/cli/src` (`check-mirror-conformance.ts:65`, `check-verification-decay.ts:88`, `mirror-conformance.test.ts:21`), so rule (5) points 3-of-3 at `cli` while this rule and the obligation point at `desktop`. Rule (5) is not wrong here; it is DEGENERATE. An instrument’s call sites are its own driver and its own test, which sit beside it by construction, so counting them merely re-reports where the file already lives and can never name the surface under obligation. Rule (5) therefore governs a LODGER — code with real consumers spread across stories — and this rule governs an INSTRUMENT; where a subtree is both, this one wins. Read that fence in the other direction too, because it costs this arc a data point: increment 3 did NOT confirm rule (5), it SET IT ASIDE, so nothing here counts as a second instance of the call-site method and the falsifier that would test it (`cli` 29 declarations / `studio` 32) is still unrun. ### FIFTH FENCE ON RULE (5) — THE FALSIFIER RAN IN `studio` AND CAME BACK IDLE: NOT HELD, NOT FAILED, NEVER ENGAGED. Added 2026-08-07 by capability-layer-coverage-arc increment 4, which took the `studio` story (31 declarations) expressly to run it. **n stays 1** — increment 2's `open-link-policy.ts` is still the only header-vs-call-sites CONFLICT in existence, and `studio` supplied no second one. THE CASE THAT LOOKED LIKE A CONFLICT IS NOT ONE, and `story-author` refused the increment's framing on the bytes. `apps/studio/src/lib/stressLayout.ts` opens by naming ADR-0171's default-OFF `?layout=stress` map mode — an ORIGIN, which is exactly the bait rule (5) exists to catch — but lines 19-23 of that SAME comment block record that ADR-0283 D2 RETIRED that mode ('nothing on the map reaches this any more') and name the surviving caller, `overviewConstellation.ts`, by file. The header therefore does not conflict with the call sites; it CONTAINS them and agrees, and rule (5)'s aphorism (a header names ORIGIN, the call sites name JOB) presumes a header that is SILENT about the job. DECISIVELY, RULE (1) HAD ALREADY RESOLVED IT AT MAXIMUM STRENGTH, BEFORE THE IMPORT GRAPH WAS CONSULTED AT ALL: `stories/library-tech-tree-overlay/library-overview.md:156` names `apps/studio/src/lib/stressLayout.ts` BY PATH inside its `constellationLayout` contract, so the tree already said who owned it. The enumeration was 1-of-1 — a fraction fence (i) says settles NOTHING by arithmetic — so a session moving on that count alone would have reached the right owner for a reason this rule's own fence disclaims. THAT IS NOT EVIDENCE FOR THE RULE, and banking it as a second instance is precisely the corruption increment 3 was corrected for. THE STRUCTURAL FINDING, which is the durable part and is the reason to expect scarcity rather than bad luck: this house writes long headers AND MAINTAINS THEM — ADR-0251 corrected `overviewConstellation.ts`'s stale comment, and ADR-0283's retirement was written into three files in one pass. A header kept current CANNOT have drifted from its call sites, and rule (5) only does work once it has. So `open-link-policy.ts` may be an EXCEPTION rather than the first of a class, and the method may be close to unfalsifiable in this corpus. FOR `guidance-curator`, WHOSE DECISION THIS BLOCKS: treat the lodger call-site rule as UNRECONFIRMED at n=1, and weigh whether a rule stuck at n=1 should graduate into every session's guidance at all — that is now a live question, not a formality awaiting a second data point. Do NOT hunt the falsifier in `studio`: measured across all 31 declarations, none is a conflict case. `cli` is the only untried candidate, and it should be entered with the EXPECTATION (not the measurement) that it will not supply one either, since fence 4 above already makes rule (5) degenerate for the gate instruments that dominate `packages/cli/src`.

baseline.$comment: The measurement `storytree ownership` prints its trend against — the evidence base a future blocking rung would have to argue from. Re-record it deliberately, not on every edit: a moved baseline erases the trend it exists to show.

subtrees.$section_cli: packages/cli — the verb surface. Most modules here FRONT another organism's competence, so the honest owner is that organism's capability, not the `cli` story: `drift.ts` is binding-staleness's, `tree.ts` is notice-board's, `deploy-health.ts` is studio-cloud's. What is left over — the gate rungs, drains, projections and doctors — has no capability anywhere in the tree, and is declared at story grain so the report counts it.
subtrees.$section_cli_residual: STORY GRAIN, and each one is a capability the tree does not have. These are the gate rungs, drains, generated-view builders and doctors — real competences with no addressable unit finer than the `cli` story to claim. Counted as story-grain by `storytree ownership`; see the block $comment.
subtrees.$section_drive: packages/drive — the shared build/orchestrate drivers (ADR-0112). Nearly every module is a named drive-machinery capability or the driver half of another story's capability; the residue is composition glue.
subtrees.$section_orchestrator: packages/orchestrator — the deterministic spine and the proof ruler. The best-mapped package in the repo: drive-machinery decomposed the spine capability-by-capability, so almost every file has a real owner one grain below the story.
subtrees.$section_agent: packages/agent — the leaf executors behind the PhaseAuthor seam.
subtrees.$section_library: packages/library — the knowledge tier. `src/store` is the seam (seed entry); the root barrel splits by competence between the library story's own capabilities and the UAT/proof-binding stories that host their pure computes here.
subtrees.$section_ports_and_boards: The two root ports and the two small board/member organisms. Each is one competence end to end, so a directory-grain entry IS the honest grain here rather than a shortcut.
subtrees.$section_studio_server: apps/studio/server — the shared API route table. Owned largely by studio-cloud, library-review and studio-members capabilities rather than by the `studio` surface story.
subtrees.$section_studio_components: apps/studio/src/components — the renderer. The Library lens components map one-to-one onto library-tech-tree-overlay capabilities; the forest map does not. TreeView.tsx is declared at STORY grain deliberately: SEVEN units name it, so no single capability is responsible for it, and that is the ADR-0317 non-injectivity finding standing in one file.
subtrees.$section_studio_shell: apps/studio — the SPA shell, the Playwright/Vitest configs and the story-UAT spec.
subtrees.$section_desktop: apps/desktop — the thick client. The backend routes are desktop capabilities one-to-one; the Electron shell, keychain and credential ports are the two credential/shell capabilities; `src/apply` (the ADR-0117 brokered rebuild loop) has no capability yet.
subtrees.$section_world_and_art: The render core, the shared app surface, the R3F website engine and the art factory.
subtrees.$section_uat_organisms: The UAT-witness organisms — the best-decomposed corner of the tree, where nearly every file is its own capability.
subtrees.$section_traversal: The four context-traversal organisms — every non-barrel file is a named capability.

hostedStories.$comment: ADR-0192 decision 2 — the packages-forward GRANDFATHER register: the FROZEN list of stories whose unit proof-bound sources (proof.real.sourceFile + literal sourceGlobs) already lived inside ANOTHER story's building (a foreign packages/<x> or apps/<x> dir) at adoption (2026-07-13), derived mechanically via the landlord rule's evidence (rule 5, PR #720). check-boundaries.ts passes this register's keys to the pure judge (packages/cli/src/boundaries.ts): a hosted story ABSENT from the register is REFUSED regardless of declared edges (a NEW story's code lives in its OWN workspace package — packages-forward), and a register entry with NO hosting evidence is a STALE violation (remove it) — so the register is the self-pruning migration worklist (ADR-0192 decision 3: migrate one story at a time, whole footprint at once). Entries only ever LEAVE as stories migrate; ADDING one is a loud, owner-reviewed diff. Every entry below already carries a declared host edge (the increment-1 remediation), so the landlord rule is green over them.
